items.prompt: Black to move. The bishop on g5 attacks the knight on f6. Find a good reply.

claims.statement: These moves (e6, Nbd7, Nc6, Bd7) are all within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move (depth 16).

hints: Which of your pieces does the bishop attack, and how many pieces defend it?
One reply opens the f8 bishop's path; others add a defender to f6 or develop.
Play the e-pawn one square, or develop a piece.
items.explain: The bishop on g5 attacks the knight on f6, which stands in front of the queen. Black can answer with the e-pawn, which frees the f8 bishop and guards d5, or develop with the b8 knight (adding a defender to f6), the b8 knight to c6, or the c8 bishop. The engine puts e6, Nbd7, Nc6, Bd7 within 40 centipawns of its best move at depth 16, with ...e6 on top; this lesson follows ...e6.

items.prompt: White to move. Black's pawn on e6 left the square e5 open for ...d5 and later ...e5 ideas. Find the pawn move that controls e5.

claims.statement: Exactly one pawn move attacks e5: f4.
After f4 one white pawn attacks e5.
f4 is within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move (depth 16).

hints: Which pawn can reach a square from which it attacks e5?
Only the pawn on the f-file can.
Play the f-pawn two squares.
items.explain: A pawn on f4 attacks e5, so Black cannot use that square freely, and it also makes room for the queen on the third rank and for long castling. The engine ranks f4 first at depth 16.

items.prompt: White to move. White wants to castle long soon, so the queen has to leave d1. Find the queen move.

claims.statement: Qf3 is within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move (depth 16).

hints: After the queen leaves d1, which squares between king and rook are free?
Two queen moves look natural; one keeps an eye on g4 and the f-file.
Play the queen to the third rank.
items.explain: The queen leaves d1 so that the king can castle long, and on f3 it covers e4 and g4 and keeps the bishop on f1 free. On e2 it would block that bishop. The engine rates Qf3 first and Qe2 at least 40 centipawns lower at depth 16.

feedback_by_move.d1e2: The queen leaves d1, but on e2 it blocks the bishop on f1. Black gets time for ...b5.

Castle long.

items.prompt: Black to move. White's bishop has taken the knight on f6. Which recapture keeps Black's pawn structure and leaves the bishop on e7 guarding the king?

claims.statement: ...Nxf6 and ...Bxf6 are both within 60 centipawns of the engine's best move (depth 16).
...gxf6 is at least 50 centipawns worse than the engine's best move (depth 16).

hints: Three pieces can recapture on f6. Which one damages Black's pawn structure?
A pawn recapture doubles the f-pawns. Of the two piece recaptures, one keeps the bishop at home.
Take with the knight from d7.
items.explain: The knight from d7 recaptures and keeps both the pawn structure and the bishop on e7 at home to guard the king. The pawn recapture doubles Black's f-pawns and opens the g-file in front of the king; the bishop recapture is also playable but moves the king's defender. The engine puts both piece recaptures within 60 centipawns of its best (their order changes with the search settings) and the pawn recapture at least 50 centipawns lower at depth 16 [V].

feedback_by_move.g7f6: The pawn recapture doubles the f-pawns and opens the g-file in front of the king that White is attacking.
feedback_by_move.e7f6: The bishop recapture is playable, but it takes the bishop away from the defence of the king, which White is about to attack.
